gap_detail.statement: Choosing the wrong task_type for the model head
gap_detail.source_fix: Set task_type to match the head (CAUSAL_LM, SEQ_2_SEQ_LM, SEQ_CLS, TOKEN_CLS, QUESTION_ANS, FEATURE_EXTRACTION)
gap_detail.quote: `task_type` must match the head: `TaskType.CAUSAL_LM`, `TaskType.SEQ_2_SEQ_LM`, `TaskType.SEQ_CLS`, `TaskType.TOKEN_CLS`
gap_detail.reason: loraconfig-core-parameters is scoped explicitly to r/lora_alpha/target_modules/init and does not cover task_type/head matching; no unit teaches the CAUSAL_LM/SEQ_CLS-style head enum.

gap_detail.statement: AdaLoRA rank schedule desyncs from the actual run length
gap_detail.source_fix: Set total_step to the actual number of optimizer steps; a wrong value desynchronizes the schedule
gap_detail.quote: Set `total_step` to the actual number of optimizer steps in your run; an incorrect value desynchronizes the rank schedule.
gap_detail.reason: No unit teaches AdaLoRA's total_step parameter; choose-peft-method only decides whether to use AdaLoRA and loraconfig-core-parameters is scoped to r/alpha/target_modules/init, so the schedule-desync fix is uncovered.

gap_detail.statement: Model is too large for one GPU even quantized, but multiple GPUs are available
gap_detail.source_fix: Use DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 for the largest models, FSDP for medium models
gap_detail.quote: DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 for the largest models; FSDP for medium models
gap_detail.reason: multi-gpu-peft-scaling is the only ZeRO-3/FSDP unit but delivery.stages=[generate] excludes the issue's explore stage; choose-peft-method only routes to a single 'multi-GPU sharding' bucket, not the ZeRO-3-vs-FSDP fix.

gap_detail.statement: Task needs an RL/preference-optimization loop (PPO, DPO, reward models)
gap_detail.source_fix: Use trl for the RL loop; PEFT only supplies the adapter that trl trains
gap_detail.quote: For the RL/preference-optimization loop itself (PPO, DPO, reward models) — use `trl` instead; PEFT supplies the adapter that trl trains.
gap_detail.reason: 'use trl' exists only as avoid_when redirects; for an actual RL-loop situation the carrying units (choose-peft-method, lora-fine-tune) are ruled out by that very avoid_when, so no unit is delivered.

gap_detail.statement: Task needs high-throughput production serving of the merged model
gap_detail.source_fix: Use a dedicated inference engine (e.g. vLLM), not PEFT
gap_detail.quote: For high-throughput production serving of the merged model — use a dedicated inference engine (e.g. vLLM) instead.
gap_detail.reason: 'use vLLM' exists only as avoid_when redirects; choose-peft-method and load-inference-adapter are contraindication-filtered out for a high-throughput-serving situation, so nothing surfaces the fix.

gap_detail.statement: Training is unstable at higher LoRA ranks
gap_detail.source_fix: Enable use_rslora for rank-stabilized scaling (lora_alpha/sqrt(r))
gap_detail.quote: use rank-stabilized scaling (`lora_alpha / sqrt(r)` instead of `lora_alpha / r`), which stabilizes training at higher ranks.
gap_detail.reason: use_rslora is a separate stability flag, not one of the four enumerated core params; loraconfig-core-parameters (scaling=lora_alpha) does not teach rank-stabilized alpha/sqrt(r) scaling.

gap_detail.statement: A freshly-initialized head (e.g. classifier) also needs training, not just the adapter
gap_detail.source_fix: Add it to modules_to_save so it trains fully and is saved alongside the adapter
gap_detail.quote: extra modules (e.g. a freshly-initialized classifier head) to train fully and save alongside the adapter.
gap_detail.reason: modules_to_save (train+save a fresh head fully) is distinct from target_modules and absent from every unit; no unit addresses fully-training an added classifier head.

gap_detail.statement: Prompt-tuning TEXT init text doesn't fit the configured virtual-token count
gap_detail.source_fix: Ensure prompt_tuning_init_text fits within num_virtual_tokens (and set tokenizer_name_or_path)
gap_detail.quote: `prompt_tuning_init_text` is tokenized and must fit within `num_virtual_tokens`
gap_detail.reason: The num_virtual_tokens/init-text fit is soft-prompt config; loraconfig-core-parameters is ruled out by its soft-prompt avoid_when and nothing else addresses it.

gap_detail.statement: Verifying the adapter actually wrapped the model
gap_detail.source_fix: Call print_trainable_parameters() — trainable % should be small (often <1%)
gap_detail.quote: `print_trainable_parameters()` is the fastest sanity check that the adapter wrapped correctly — the trainable % should be small (often <1%).
gap_detail.reason: print_trainable_parameters lives in the LoRA setup procedure (lora-fine-tune), but that unit is generate/refine only and hard-filtered at debug; the only debug-eligible unit (qlora-small-gpu) is topically about 4-bit fitting, not adapter-wrap verification.

gap_detail.statement: Combining ZeRO-3 + QLoRA to fit a 70B model on 2×40GB GPUs
gap_detail.source_fix: Meet the version floor: bitsandbytes>=0.43.3, accelerate>=1.0.1, transformers>4.44.2, trl>0.11.4, peft>0.13.0, zero3_init_flag true
gap_detail.quote: Requires `bitsandbytes>=0.43.3`, `accelerate>=1.0.1`, `transformers>4.44.2`, `trl>0.11.4`, `peft>0.13.0`
gap_detail.reason: No unit addresses the specific dependency version floor (bitsandbytes/accelerate/transformers/trl/peft pins); multi-gpu-peft-scaling shares the ZeRO-3 topic but its scope is training mechanics, not environment/version prerequisites.

gap_detail.statement: Need to train a large model on a single GPU
gap_detail.source_fix: Use ZeRO-3 with offload_optimizer_device: cpu and offload_param_device: cpu to offload state to CPU
gap_detail.quote: To train a large model on one GPU, offload optimizer and parameter state to CPU.
gap_detail.reason: No unit teaches ZeRO-3 CPU-offload for a single GPU; qlora-small-gpu shares the 'fit large model on small GPU' topic but its fix is 4-bit quantization not CPU offload, and multi-gpu-peft-scaling requires multiple GPUs (avoid_when: model fits on one GPU).

gap_detail.statement: Running generate() during inference inside a custom (non-Trainer) ZeRO-3 loop
gap_detail.source_fix: Detect ZeRO-3 to gate generate() and use Accelerate's backward
gap_detail.quote: In a custom (non-Trainer) loop, detect ZeRO-3 to gate `generate()` during inference, and use Accelerate's `backward`
gap_detail.reason: multi-gpu-peft-scaling overlaps on the generate stage but only covers driving sharded training via Accelerate/launch config; it does not address gating generate() or using Accelerate's backward inside a custom non-Trainer ZeRO-3 loop.

gap_detail.statement: Estimating whether a given model+method fits on a specific GPU
gap_detail.source_fix: Use the referenced fits — Llama-2-7B QLoRA+TRL on 16GB, 20B RLHF+PEFT+TRL on 24GB
gap_detail.quote: Llama-2-7B with QLoRA + TRL fits on a 16GB GPU; 20B-parameter RLHF with PEFT + TRL fits on a 24GB consumer GPU
gap_detail.reason: No unit holds the quantitative VRAM-fit references (7B QLoRA@16GB, 20B RLHF@24GB); choose-peft-method is explore-eligible but only gives method trade-offs, not fit estimation, and qlora-small-gpu (memory unit) isn't eligible at explore.

gap_detail.statement: Need the fewest trainable params / fastest to train
gap_detail.source_fix: Use prompt tuning
gap_detail.quote: Fewest parameters, fastest to train → **prompt tuning**.
gap_detail.reason: No unit teaches soft-prompt methods; choose-peft-method lumps all soft prompts as one bucket and never resolves prompt-tuning as the fewest-params pick.

gap_detail.statement: Need soft prompts that touch every layer for more capacity
gap_detail.source_fix: Use prefix tuning
gap_detail.quote: Soft prompts that touch every layer (more capacity) → **prefix tuning**.
gap_detail.reason: No unit names or distinguishes prefix tuning; the within-soft-prompt capacity choice is absent from the compiled inventory.

gap_detail.statement: Need to preserve the base model's behavior (e.g. subject-driven image gen, ControlNet/DreamBooth)
gap_detail.source_fix: Use OFT / BOFT orthogonal fine-tuning
gap_detail.quote: Preserving the base model's behavior (e.g. subject-driven image generation, ControlNet/DreamBooth) → **OFT / BOFT**.
gap_detail.reason: OFT/BOFT and the base-preservation use case appear in no unit; choose-peft-method's family list omits orthogonal fine-tuning entirely.

gap_detail.statement: Prompt tuning converges slowly from random init
gap_detail.source_fix: Initialize from real task text with PromptTuningInit.TEXT for faster convergence
gap_detail.quote: Initializing the prompt from real task text (`PromptTuningInit.TEXT`) usually converges faster than random init.
gap_detail.reason: PromptTuningInit.TEXT is soft-prompt config; loraconfig-core-parameters explicitly avoid_when soft prompts and no other unit covers prompt-tuning init.

gap_detail.statement: Prefix tuning is unstable to train
gap_detail.source_fix: Add the optional MLP reparameterization via prefix_projection to stabilize training
gap_detail.quote: An optional MLP reparameterization (`prefix_projection`) stabilizes training.
gap_detail.reason: prefix_projection stabilization is prefix-tuning-specific and absent from every unit's content.

gap_detail.statement: Plain prompt tuning underfits
gap_detail.source_fix: Switch to prefix tuning when prompt tuning underfits
gap_detail.quote: prefer prefix tuning over plain prompt tuning when prompt tuning underfits.
gap_detail.reason: Choosing prefix over prompt tuning is a within-soft-prompt decision that choose-peft-method (family-level only) cannot resolve.

gap_detail.statement: Deciding when P-tuning is the right soft-prompt method
gap_detail.source_fix: Reach for P-tuning on natural-language understanding (classification) tasks
gap_detail.quote: P-tuning was designed for natural-language understanding (classification) tasks; reach for it there.
gap_detail.reason: P-tuning and the NLU-task heuristic are named in no unit; the soft-prompt bucket in choose-peft-method does not distinguish P-tuning.

gap_detail.statement: Have multiple related tasks and want cross-task transfer
gap_detail.source_fix: Use multitask prompt tuning to share a prompt across source tasks then specialize
gap_detail.quote: Use it when you have multiple related tasks and want transfer between them.
gap_detail.reason: Multitask prompt tuning and cross-task transfer appear in no compiled unit.

covered_detail.statement: User wants parameter-efficient fine-tuning but hasn't chosen a method
covered_detail.source_fix: Default to LoRA; use DoRA/AdaLoRA for higher quality; IA3 or soft prompts when you need the fewest trainable params
covered_detail.quote: LoRA as the default; DoRA/AdaLoRA for higher quality at slightly more cost; IA3 or soft prompts (prefix/P-tuning) when you need the fewest trainable params
covered_detail.reason: choose-peft-method is explore-eligible and its when-clause 'a PEFT method has not yet been chosen' is exactly this default-selection routing (LoRA vs DoRA/IA3/soft prompts).

covered_detail.statement: The base model does not fit in VRAM on a single GPU (<24GB)
covered_detail.source_fix: Use QLoRA — load the base in 4-bit and train a LoRA adapter on top
covered_detail.quote: QLoRA — load the base in 4-bit and train a LoRA adapter on top
covered_detail.reason: qlora-small-gpu overlaps the issue's generate stage and its when 'base+LoRA+optimizer does not fit on a single <24GB GPU' is the exact 4-bit-base + LoRA fix.

covered_detail.statement: Deciding how to deploy the tuned model — single merged model vs serving multiple tasks from one base
covered_detail.source_fix: merge_and_unload for zero-overhead single-model inference; keep adapter separate and swap with set_adapter for multi-task serving
covered_detail.quote: `merge_and_unload` into one model for zero-overhead inference (LoRA-family only, not on a quantized base); keep the adapter separate and swap with `set_adapter`
covered_detail.reason: load-inference-adapter overlaps generate; it covers both optional merge and serving-multiple-tasks-by-swapping, which is exactly the merge-vs-swap deployment decision.

covered_detail.statement: Reaching for QLoRA/4-bit even when the bf16 base already fits in memory
covered_detail.source_fix: Use plain LoRA when memory isn't the constraint — 4-bit only adds overhead and a fragile grad path
covered_detail.quote: 4-bit adds dequantization overhead and a more fragile k-bit grad path, for no benefit when memory isn't the constraint.
covered_detail.reason: choose-peft-method is explore-eligible and its when names the memory trade-off; the LoRA-vs-QLoRA memory boundary (plain LoRA unless memory-constrained) is squarely its routing remit.

covered_detail.statement: Setting up a QLoRA run on a 4-bit-loaded base
covered_detail.source_fix: Call prepare_model_for_kbit_training on the loaded model before attaching LoRA
covered_detail.quote: Step 3: Call `prepare_model_for_kbit_training` on the loaded model
covered_detail.reason: qlora-small-gpu overlaps generate and its 'make it trainable' step on the 4-bit base is the prepare_model_for_kbit_training call this issue needs.

covered_detail.statement: Wanting to merge the adapter for zero-overhead inference
covered_detail.source_fix: merge_and_unload works for LoRA-family adapters only, and not on a quantized base
covered_detail.quote: Optionally call `merge_and_unload()` to fold weights in for zero inference overhead (LoRA-family only, not on a quantized base)
covered_detail.reason: load-inference-adapter overlaps generate/refine and carries the exact constraint in its avoid_when: merge_and_unload is LoRA-family-only and not supported on a quantized base.

covered_detail.statement: Attaching a saved adapter to its base model to generate
covered_detail.source_fix: Use PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, adapter_path), or AutoPeftModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained for one-call loading
covered_detail.quote: Attach the adapter with `PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, adapter_path)`
covered_detail.reason: load-inference-adapter overlaps generate and its core is attaching a saved adapter to its base (PeftModel.from_pretrained) and generating.

covered_detail.statement: Code uses deprecated prepare_model_for_int8_training
covered_detail.source_fix: Replace with prepare_model_for_kbit_training
covered_detail.quote: **`prepare_model_for_int8_training`** (deprecated in 0.4.0) — use `prepare_model_for_kbit_training` instead.
covered_detail.reason: qlora-small-gpu overlaps debug and its k-bit trainable-prep step is prepare_model_for_kbit_training — the current API this deprecation redirects to, in the quantized-training context where int8_training appears.

covered_detail.statement: Passing load_in_8bit/load_in_4bit directly to from_pretrained (deprecated)
covered_detail.source_fix: Pass a BitsAndBytesConfig via quantization_config instead
covered_detail.quote: use `BitsAndBytesConfig` passed via `quantization_config` instead.
covered_detail.reason: qlora-small-gpu overlaps debug and its 4-bit base-loading step uses BitsAndBytesConfig via quantization_config, the current API replacing the deprecated load_in_8bit/4bit kwargs.

covered_detail.statement: Writing a fresh LoRA fine-tuning script
covered_detail.source_fix: Build a LoraConfig (task_type, r, lora_alpha, target_modules), wrap with get_peft_model, train, save adapter
covered_detail.quote: build a `LoraConfig` (`task_type`, `r`, `lora_alpha`, `target_modules`), wrap it with `get_peft_model`
covered_detail.reason: lora-fine-tune is the generate-stage procedure for building a LoraConfig, wrapping with get_peft_model, training, and saving the adapter — a direct match.

covered_detail.statement: Picking the LoRA rank r
covered_detail.source_fix: Start low and raise r only if the adapter underfits
covered_detail.quote: Higher `r` adds capacity at the cost of more parameters; start low and raise only if the adapter underfits.
covered_detail.reason: The rank knob (r/capacity) is core to loraconfig-core-parameters, which is refine-eligible and covers 'deciding rank' including start-low-raise-if-underfit.

covered_detail.statement: Choosing lora_alpha relative to r
covered_detail.source_fix: Use the lora_alpha = 2*r heuristic to keep the effective scale at 2
covered_detail.quote: A common heuristic is `lora_alpha = 2 * r`
covered_detail.reason: lora_alpha (scaling) is one of the four core knobs; unit is generate-eligible and governs the alpha-vs-r scaling heuristic.

covered_detail.statement: Not specifying target_modules in LoraConfig
covered_detail.source_fix: PEFT applies a model-type default (often attention query/value projections) when omitted
covered_detail.quote: If omitted, PEFT applies a model-type default (often the attention query/value projections).
covered_detail.reason: target_modules (placement) is a core knob covered by the unit at generate, including the omitted/model-default behavior.

covered_detail.statement: Training converges slowly from zero-init adapters
covered_detail.source_fix: Use PiSSA/OLoRA/LoftQ init strings to initialize from a decomposition of the base weights for faster convergence
covered_detail.quote: PiSSA/OLoRA/LoftQ-style strings to initialize from a decomposition of the base weights for faster convergence.
covered_detail.reason: init (init_lora_weights) is the 4th core knob; unit is refine-eligible and covers PiSSA/OLoRA/LoftQ-style initialization.

covered_detail.statement: Want better-than-LoRA quality at low rank
covered_detail.source_fix: Enable DoRA via use_dora=True flag on LoraConfig (not a separate config class)
covered_detail.quote: It typically improves over plain LoRA at low ranks. It is not a separate config class — it is a flag on `LoraConfig`
covered_detail.reason: choose-peft-method is explore/generate-eligible and its decision boundaries explicitly cover picking DoRA for better quality at low rank.

covered_detail.statement: Considering DoRA when memory/speed is tight
covered_detail.source_fix: Account for DoRA's added magnitude params — slower and more memory than plain LoRA at the same r
covered_detail.quote: DoRA adds the magnitude parameters, so it is somewhat slower and uses more memory than plain LoRA at the same `r`.
covered_detail.reason: choose-peft-method is explore-eligible and weighs memory/speed trade-offs across adapter families, which is exactly the DoRA magnitude-param cost consideration.

covered_detail.statement: Deciding whether AdaLoRA fits the goal
covered_detail.source_fix: Use AdaLoRA for LoRA-level quality under a tight parameter budget, letting it allocate per-layer rank
covered_detail.quote: AdaLoRA is most useful when you want LoRA-level quality under a tight parameter budget
covered_detail.reason: choose-peft-method is a method-selection reference that explicitly names DoRA/AdaLoRA and weighs quality vs parameter-budget; eligible at explore.

covered_detail.statement: Want LoRA-like quality with even fewer params and no merge into weights
covered_detail.source_fix: Use IA3
covered_detail.quote: LoRA-like quality with even fewer params, no merge into weights → **IA3**.
covered_detail.reason: choose-peft-method explicitly enumerates IA3 as a boundary for LoRA-like quality at a smaller parameter budget; eligible at explore, no avoid_when triggered.

covered_detail.statement: Configuring 4-bit quantization for QLoRA
covered_detail.source_fix: Use the canonical settings — NF4 datatype, nested/double quantization, bf16/fp16 compute dtype
covered_detail.quote: The canonical QLoRA settings use the NF4 datatype, nested (double) quantization, and a bf16/fp16 compute dtype.
covered_detail.reason: qlora-small-gpu is the QLoRA 4-bit-base procedure; configuring the canonical bnb 4-bit settings is its central 'load frozen base in 4-bit' step, eligible at generate.

covered_detail.statement: Choosing the 4-bit quant type
covered_detail.source_fix: Use nf4 (QLoRA recommendation) over fp4
covered_detail.quote: `bnb_4bit_quant_type` accepts `"nf4"` (normal-float, the QLoRA recommendation) or `"fp4"`.
covered_detail.reason: Choosing the 4-bit quant type is a sub-detail of the QLoRA 4-bit loading procedure (nf4 is the canonical setting it uses); stage generate overlaps.

covered_detail.statement: Wrong bnb_4bit_compute_dtype (e.g. float32) silently slows training
covered_detail.source_fix: Use torch.bfloat16 on Ampere+ (A6000/A100), torch.float16 on older HW; never leave it at float32
covered_detail.quote: should be `torch.bfloat16` on Ampere+ GPUs (A6000, A100), or `torch.float16` on older hardware. Keeping this at float32 silently slows training.
covered_detail.reason: bnb_4bit_compute_dtype is a core knob of the QLoRA 4-bit config; qlora-small-gpu spans generate and debug, matching the issue's stages.

covered_detail.statement: Want a quantized base closer to full precision than 4-bit
covered_detail.source_fix: Set load_in_8bit instead — heavier than 4-bit but closer to full precision; rest of recipe identical
covered_detail.quote: For an 8-bit base, set `load_in_8bit` instead. This is heavier than 4-bit but closer to full precision.
covered_detail.reason: The unit's when clause explicitly covers '4-bit/8-bit quantized base loading', so the load_in_8bit alternative is in scope; generate overlaps.

covered_detail.statement: QLoRA 'trains' but loss is flat — no gradient reaches the adapters
covered_detail.source_fix: Call prepare_model_for_kbit_training (mandatory) after loading the quantized base; skipping it is the most common QLoRA failure
covered_detail.quote: Skipping it is the single most common QLoRA failure: the model "trains" but the loss is flat because no gradient reaches the adapters.
covered_detail.reason: This is the exact 'make it trainable' / k-bit grad-path step the unit centers on; unit is eligible at debug, matching the issue's debug stage.

covered_detail.statement: Ordering of gradient_checkpointing_enable relative to prepare_model_for_kbit_training
covered_detail.source_fix: Call model.gradient_checkpointing_enable() BEFORE prepare_model_for_kbit_training
covered_detail.quote: if you also call `model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()` yourself, do it **before** `prepare_model_for_kbit_training`.
covered_detail.reason: The gradient_checkpointing/prepare ordering is part of the QLoRA make-trainable setup the procedure covers; stages generate+debug overlap.

covered_detail.statement: Ordering of prepare_model_for_kbit_training relative to get_peft_model
covered_detail.source_fix: Call prepare once, immediately after loading the quantized base and before get_peft_model
covered_detail.quote: Call it once, immediately after loading the quantized base and before `get_peft_model`.
covered_detail.reason: The prepare-then-LoRA ordering is implied by the unit's sequence (load 4-bit → make trainable → train LoRA on top); eligible at generate.

covered_detail.statement: print_trainable_parameters reports 0 or an unexpectedly large trainable count
covered_detail.source_fix: The config or preparation step is wrong — fix the LoraConfig or prepare step
covered_detail.quote: If it reports 0 trainable params or an unexpectedly large count, the config or preparation step is wrong.
covered_detail.reason: Diagnosing a wrong config/prepare step via trainable-param count is the QLoRA grad-path debug the unit addresses; unit is eligible at debug.

covered_detail.statement: Setting up multi-GPU LoRA training with DeepSpeed ZeRO-3
covered_detail.source_fix: ZeRO-1/2/3 are all compatible with PEFT LoRA + bitsandbytes; drive it through Accelerate with a config file and accelerate launch
covered_detail.quote: All three stages are compatible with PEFT LoRA + `bitsandbytes`. It is driven through Accelerate
covered_detail.reason: This is exactly the unit's summary — driving sharded multi-GPU LoRA via Accelerate + launch config; generate stage overlaps and avoid_when (fits one GPU) does not apply.

covered_detail.statement: Saved ZeRO-3 adapter isn't reloadable with from_pretrained
covered_detail.source_fix: Set zero3_save_16bit_model: true so saved adapter weights are 16-bit and reloadable
covered_detail.quote: confirm `zero3_save_16bit_model: true` so the saved adapter weights are 16-bit and reloadable with `from_pretrained`.
covered_detail.reason: zero3_save_16bit_model is a launch-config setting within the unit's Accelerate 'launch config' scope; generate overlaps (debug excluded but generate suffices).

covered_detail.statement: ZeRO-3 + QLoRA: 4-bit storage dtype must match the model load dtype
covered_detail.source_fix: Set bnb_4bit_quant_storage and the model dtype to the same value (e.g. bfloat16)
covered_detail.quote: The training-code change is the 4-bit storage dtype, which must match the model load dtype
covered_detail.reason: Matching bnb_4bit_quant_storage to the model dtype is a training-code change within the ZeRO-3+QLoRA sharding workflow (when covers 'too large even quantized'); generate overlaps.

covered_detail.statement: Setting up multi-GPU LoRA training with FSDP
covered_detail.source_fix: FSDP shards params/gradients/optimizer states across processes and can offload sharded params to CPU; configure via accelerate config
covered_detail.quote: Fully Sharded Data Parallel shards parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across data-parallel processes and can offload sharded params to CPU.
covered_detail.reason: multi-gpu-peft-scaling directly teaches sharded multi-GPU LoRA training via FSDP/ZeRO-3 through Accelerate config; its generate stage overlaps the issue's generate stage and avoid_when (fits on one GPU) does not apply.
